To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CaMK2alpha is present in afferent synapses of the VML and that PTP in this pathway is dependent on the presence of CaMK2alpha.

Ca2+/cal modulin-dependent kinase II alpha subunit (CAMK2alpha) is expressed in a subset of glutamatergicsynapses in the electrosensory system of A. leptorrhyncus, and CaMK2 is required for the induction of posttetanic potentiaton at a subset of these synapses.
CaMK2 is present in the brain of the gymnotiform fish A. leptorynchus, and that it is localized to presynaptic terminals in the ventral molecular layer of the electrosensory lobe.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CaMK2 in synaptic plasticity and its relationship to Hebbian learning.
the role of the Ca2+-dependent kinase CaMK2 in the modulation of glutamate receptors in the ELL.
the molecular mechanisms underlying learning and memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaMKII is not involved in Hebbian plasticity, but it is involved in PTP.
CaMK2 is not necessary for Hebbian or non-Hebbian forms of plasticity.
CaMK2 is involved in the regulation of PTP at some but not all glutamatergigic synapses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CaMK2 alpha is a presynaptic kinase that is involved in PTP in the ELL.
the CaMK2-dependent PTP is input selective.
CaMK2 is involved in the induction of PTP in the ventral molecular layer of the electrosensory lobe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CaMK2 is not involved in the induction of PTP in DML.
CaMK2 is not a universal requirement for PTP and may be a synapse-specific requirement for this phenomenon.
CaMK2 is not required for Hebbian plasticity.
